summary: Duplicate alert suppression: POST /api/alerts returns 200 + X-Duplicate-Suppressed: true with the existing alert when an active alert with the same Title (case-insensitive) and Severity was created within a configurable window (default 15 min)

acceptance_criteria.text: On POST /api/alerts, if an active alert with the same Title (case-insensitive) and the same Severity was created within the suppression window, no new alert row is created.
A suppressed request returns 200 OK with the existing alert in the body and the response header 'X-Duplicate-Suppressed: true'.
A request with no matching recent active alert still creates the alert and returns 201 Created (with Location), without the 'X-Duplicate-Suppressed' header.
The suppression window (minutes) is read from appsettings.json configuration, not hardcoded; appsettings.json provides the default of 15.
An alert with the same Title but a different Severity is not suppressed (a new alert is created).
A matching alert that is inactive is not treated as a duplicate (a new alert is created).
A matching active alert created before the start of the window (older than the configured minutes) is not treated as a duplicate (a new alert is created).

constraints: No hardcoded values: window minutes come from configuration (IOptions<AlertSuppressionOptions>, section e.g. 'AlertSuppression:DuplicateWindowMinutes'); header name and config keys as constants.
Layering: controller -> IAlertService (DTOs only) -> IAlertRepository; service must not reference EF Core. Duplicate decision lives in the service; repository only exposes a query.

Title match is case-insensitive and provider-agnostic (tests use InMemory/SQLite, prod uses SQL Server): compare trimmed title via ToLower(), as the existing 'search' filter does. Compare against the same trimmed title that ToEntity would store.
Window cutoff computed from the injected TimeProvider (UtcNow - window), never DateTime.UtcNow; CreatedDate is stored in UTC.

Duplicate lookup must be a parameterized EF query (no raw SQL), AsNoTracking not required since the entity is mapped straight to the response; return the most recent match when several exist; include Tags so ToResponse is complete (AlertResponse has Tags).

Changing IAlertService.CreateAsync's return type and the AlertManagementService constructor breaks existing tests (AlertsControllerTests.Create_*, AlertManagementServiceTests constructor and CreateAsync_*); /unit-testing must update them. /implement-story therefore builds only the API project, not the solution.
Invalid configuration (window <= 0) must fail closed/safely: validate options at startup (e.g. [Range] + ValidateDataAnnotations/ValidateOnStart) rather than silently suppressing everything.

Check-then-insert is not atomic; concurrent identical requests can still create two rows. No unique constraint is feasible (time-windowed rule); accepted limitation, no DB schema change / migration for this story.
Do not log the alert Title/Description beyond what existing code logs (log alert id, severity only).
coverage_goals: Behavior coverage of AC1-AC7 incl. window boundary (inside vs. just outside), case-insensitive title match, different severity, inactive match, 200+header vs 201 without header, and window read from options (not a constant).
unresolved_questions: Config key/section name not specified: assumed 'AlertSuppression:DuplicateWindowMinutes' with default 15 in appsettings.json. Confirm.
Should an incoming request with IsActive=false be suppressed by a matching active alert? Assumed yes (rule keys only on the existing alert's state, Title and Severity). Confirm.
Window boundary: assumed an alert created exactly 15 minutes ago still counts (CreatedDate >= now - window). Confirm.
Is a window of 0 meant to disable suppression? Assumed options validation requires >= 1 (no disable switch) unless confirmed otherwise.
